project.tagline: Build what the camera can judge.

activeBuild.brief: Round 017 keeps the shoulder, far-low-left elbow, and inward-grip anchors fixed while relaxing exactly one impossible Round016 rule: only protected pixels inside the closed anchor triangle and existing limb corridors, dilated 62 pixels, become editable. The builder must restore a 24-pixel grip disk, freeze every pixel outside that revised mask, and produce one connected anatomical V around a clear head-sized pale wedge. A real Unity gate is now mandatory; the fresh Round016 run proved the toolchain works but also proved Nyra is not integrated.
facts: P00 is accepted as infrastructure; its blind visual baseline remains an explicit 28.33–76.67 loss.

Round 001 is mechanically reproducible: two independent critic reruns matched all six filed image hashes, P10 validation passed, focused EditMode passed 8/8, the full suite passed 14/14, and the P00 aggregate stayed byte-identical.
The randomized blind judge scored our round-001 frame 9/60 and Reference 09 49/60; the independent critic scored ours 10/60 and the reference 51/60.
Round 002 passed its mechanical export gates but failed visual preflight at 5/13. The decisive frame exposed torn and detached combat hands, so it never entered Unity.
A fresh-context critic scored round 003 at 6/13 with only 4/8 mandatory checks. The source package is a visual NO-GO and Unity was never launched.

Round 003 passed anatomy, face, feet, joint continuity, neutral coverage, and diagnostic coverage; it failed hands and grip, costume, weapon contact, materials, LOD0 budget, combat pose, and authored identity.

Two isolated Blender reruns matched semantic structure, topology, materials, and weights, but exact artifact determinism failed at 0/16 hashes for repository-to-run and 0/16 between runs. The round-003 audit also omitted its Combat FBX because its record key collided with the combat PNG.
A separate 80-deform-bone export prototype proved structural rig feasibility, but shoulder, elbow, wrist, thumb, finger, and facial-deformation hard gates remain unresolved; it is not combat-ready.

Round 004 mechanically delivered a lawful static Rain-derived source, five FBXs, nine diagnostics, and an 88,036-triangle LOD0, but a fresh critic rejected it at 7/13 with only 4/8 mandatory checks. Unity was never launched.

Round 004 passed anatomy, face, feet, joint continuity, LOD0, neutral coverage, and diagnostic coverage. It failed the second complete hand enclosure, premium costume construction, weapon function, material separation, combat intent, and unmistakable close-range AAA identity.
The single biggest gap is exact: the costume still reads as a toy-like procedural slab-and-tube assembly rather than believable, layered, worn, functional AAA warrior gear.

Two isolated Round 004 reruns matched all 26 frozen input hashes and canonical geometry, topology, UVs, materials, assignments, transforms, bounds, and near-pixel imagery. Exact output determinism still failed: only the 22 copied textures matched among 39 physical outputs.
All five Round 004 FBXs contain one broken absolute texture reference and leak the source path. The supplied validator missed this because it checks image resolution only in the authored blend.

Round 005 delivered a lawful Blender Studio Einar-derived static source, four static FBXs, nine 1600px diagnostics, and a fresh clean-import proof. Required credit is Einar Rig (CC-BY) Blender Foundation | studio.blender.org.

A fresh-context critic rejected Round 005 at 6/13 with only 4/8 mandatory checks. The benchmark was preferred in all 7/7 blinded comparisons, Unity remained locked, and no actual game capture was performed.

Round 005 passed anatomy, authored face and hair, grounded feet, joint continuity, LOD0 budget, and diagnostic coverage. It failed the two-hand hilt enclosure, premium warrior costume, weapon function, portable materials, combat intent, neutral modeling coverage, and unmistakable premium anime-warrior identity.

The single biggest gap is core authorship and identity: the delivery still reads as the licensed Einar civilian mechanic in workwear with attached props, not an unmistakable premium authored anime warrior at the God of War Ragnarok benchmark level.
Factory-state validation semantically passed all 4/4 static imports at 85,096 / 47,615 / 25,484 LOD triangles, but texture portability and source-to-reimport material parity both failed.

The Round 005 release-sanitization follow-up passed: checkout-specific metadata was removed without changing the judged visual payload, and factory-state validation now reproduces the audit, clean-import report, and reimport diagnostic byte-for-byte.

Round 006 filed three original 2D concept images only, not gameplay, 3D, or game-ready evidence. A fresh critic rejected the set at 55/100 against an 85 threshold, the critical category floor failed, and the candidate met the benchmark bar in 0/6 blinded comparisons.

Paid 3D generation was not authorized and Unity was not entered for Round 006. The single biggest gap is benchmark-level authored identity: the generic dark armored-anime swordswoman lacks a unique, function-led visual thesis.

Round 007 filed two accepted original 2D concept sheets and one clearly labeled rejected grip diagnostic only. A fresh critic denied paid 3D generation at 62/100 against an 85 threshold, failed the category floor, and found the candidate met the benchmark bar in 2/6 comparisons against 5/6 required.

Round 007 has no accepted combat-grip proof, gameplay, 3D asset, game-ready evidence, or Unity capture. Its single biggest gap is the absence of one accepted identity-preserving combat image that unambiguously proves both complete hands closed on separated regions of the same hilt.

Round 008 generated four bounded original 2D contact candidates. The builder froze them fail-closed under a strict clean-negative-space rule, but a fresh critic independently found candidate 04 visually unambiguous and promoted a byte-identical accepted contact copy without regenerating the art.

Round 008 passed its isolated same-hilt contact objective, raising functional grip to 8/10, but the complete pack still failed at 68/100, a 5/10 observed category floor, and only 3/6 benchmark-level comparisons against 5/6 required. Paid 3D generation and Unity remain locked.

Round 009 materially improved layered cloth, ceramic, metal, and copper separation while preserving the accepted identity, engineering anchors, one weapon, and solved same-hilt grip. A fresh critic nevertheless rejected the isolated mythic-force target at 71/100, a 6/10 floor, and 2/6 benchmark comparisons.

Round 010 removed samurai-adjacent tassets and historical odachi curvature, introduced a non-historical storm-shear, preserved identity and contact, and improved the rear toe pivot plus heavy-right-leg load. A fresh critic still rejected the signature event.

The Round 010 composite scored 68/100 against 85, failed the category floor at 6/10, and met the benchmark bar in only 2/6 comparisons against 5/6 required. The single gap is a mechanically unified violent deceleration chain rather than another wide posed greatsword hold.

Round 011 filed four bounded original 2D keyframes driven by an original public-safe pose guide. Candidate 04 materially improved the chest-height hilt, external upper-right blade mass, heavy right load column, airborne rear heel, toe skid, and coherent secondary lag, but it also introduced two-tail hair drift and exaggerated blade and boot masses.

The fresh Round 011 critic rejected the isolated kinetic-chain target at 62/100, a 5/10 category floor, and 2/6 benchmark comparisons against 5/6 required. Both scapulae and arms still advance as a paired reach, so blade mass does not resolve through an opposing shoulder girdle and deep ribcage-pelvis C-curve as one violent stop. No integrated gameplay or player build exists for this asset; engine run and actual gameplay capture are false.

Round 012 filed four bounded original 2D upper-body mechanics attempts driven by an original public-safe guide. Candidate 04 narrowly corrected the high-right/low-left shoulder order and jaw gap while preserving widely separated complete contact, the lower-body load, rear toe skid, and external blade mass; the builder still marked the target failed.

The fresh Round 012 critic rejected the isolated Scapular Counterforce Lock at 56/100, a 3/10 category floor, and 1/6 benchmark comparisons against 5/6 required. The leading elbow stays long and the trailing elbow never drops down-left and returns, so the triangular push-pull mechanism is absent and the pose reads as paired hauling. No integrated gameplay or player build exists for this asset; engine run and actual gameplay capture are false.

Round 013 filed four bounded original 2D elbow-topology attempts and an original public-safe guide. Candidate 04 alone produced a compact leading-elbow fold beneath the high shoulder, but it was promoted only as failed critic evidence because the trailing arm still descends monotonically and the guide-only reconstruction materially drifted identity, design, stance, toe skid, proportions, and framing.

The fresh Round 013 critic rejected the isolated Elbow Return Triangle at 41/100, a 1/10 category floor, and 2/6 benchmark comparisons against 5/6 required. The trailing elbow never becomes the far down-left lowest external vertex, the forearm never reverses up-right to the inward hand, and the pale triangle cannot exist. No integrated gameplay or player build exists for this asset; engine run and actual gameplay capture are false.

Round 014 filed four bounded original 2D trailing-arm attempts and an original public-safe guide. Candidate 04 alone created a conspicuous far-low-left outer bend and a short up-right reversal, but the builder marked it failed because the hand drifted outward, the hilt construction changed, and hilt/rear-leg content occupied the required pale wedge.

The fresh Round 014 critic rejected the isolated Trailing Return Wedge at 41/100, a 0/10 category floor, and 2/6 benchmark comparisons against 5/6 required. The arm-bounded return wedge is absent: the abbreviated forearm collapses into the altered hilt and rear leg, leaving the hand outward and no clean untouched head-sized pale triangle. No integrated gameplay or player build exists for this asset; engine run and actual gameplay capture are false.

Round 015 filed four bounded original 2D image-generation attempts, twelve raw/initial/protected outputs, an original public-safe guide, two deterministic hard-mask families, and a protected composite. Candidate 04 protected preserves all 1,544,522 frozen pixels with zero mismatches and restores the exact original grip and complete hilt, but the generated limb collapses to a monotonic reach and retains a residual sliver.

The fresh Round 015 critic rejected the isolated Inward Return Mask at 40/100, a 0/10 category floor, and 2/6 benchmark comparisons against 5/6 required. The required two-segment trailing-arm topology is absent: there is no far-low-left elbow, no separate steep up-right forearm return, and therefore no uninterrupted head-sized pale wedge. No Round015 integration, gameplay controller, build scene, or player build exists; engine run and actual gameplay capture are false.

Round 016 filed four original isolated-limb attempts, four complete deterministic key/map/composite/protected lineages, an exact-anchor guide, protection-zone diagnostics, and one builder-promoted failed frame. Candidate 04 hit shoulder, elbow, and grip with effectively zero transform residual, but protection removed 54,019 of 77,360 corridor pixels and left only a severed shoulder stump plus floating shard.

The fresh Round 016 critic ran Unity 6000.5.4f1 successfully in an isolated copy and captured a new S01 frame and turntable. That real capture shows the obsolete low-poly Astra Vale Round001 proxy because Nyra Round016 is absent from Unity; the gate failed at 33/100, a 0/10 floor, and 0/6 blind wins.

Round 017 is active with the critic's smallest viable constraint release: unfreeze only the protected pixels inside the dilated three-anchor triangle, restore a 24-pixel grip disk, and require one 8-connected anatomical arm with a clear pale wedge. The global latest manifest remains pinned to accepted P00.

rounds.builderBrief: Generate only one isolated armored V limb, key and map it exactly to shoulder (604,472), far-low-left elbow (370,845), and inward grip (450,625), then restore every hilt and rear-leg pixel while freezing the complete Round013 authority outside the final mask.
rounds.evidence: The builder filed four original isolated-limb attempts, four complete raw/keyed/anchored/composite/protected lineages, an original exact-anchor guide, three protection/corridor diagnostics, deterministic compositor source, and one strongest failed frame. Candidate 04 hit all three anchors with effectively zero transform residual, and all 1,549,523 sealed pixels plus every hilt/rear-leg pixel remain exact, but protection removes 54,019 of 77,360 corridor pixels—including the elbow and 100% of the return centerline—so the final image is a severed shoulder stump plus floating shard. A fresh critic independently reproduced the math and pixels, then ran Unity 6000.5.4f1 successfully in an isolated copy. The actual fresh S01 and turntable show obsolete Astra Vale Round001 because Nyra Round016 is absent from the project, so the target-matched capture gate fails. The round scored 33/100, failed the category floor at 0/10, and lost all 0/6 blinded comparisons.

critic.status: TWO-SEGMENT LIMB FAIL · TARGET-MATCHED ENGINE CAPTURE FAIL
critic.scoreLabel: Fresh engine-backed gate 33/100 · threshold 95 · category floor 0/10
critic.preference: Actual Unity evidence preferred in 0/6 blinded comparisons · 5/6 required
critic.primaryGap: The accepted silhouette has no connected shoulder-to-elbow-to-grip arm: protection destroys the elbow and entire steep return, leaving a shoulder stump and floating far-low shard instead of one anatomical V and its uninterrupted pale wedge.

pieces.name: Evidence spine
pieces.outcome: A deterministic review scene, fixed-seed capture command, manifest, round ledger, and live progress surface work end to end.

pieces.name: Shoulder camera
pieces.outcome: Exploration and combat framings preserve subject scale, sightline, collision, target legibility, and authored camera presets.

pieces.name: Ground locomotion
pieces.outcome: Walk, run, pivot, stop, strafe, slope handling, and camera-relative control have grounded acceleration and readable weight.

pieces.name: Hero animation foundation
pieces.outcome: Idle, locomotion, pivots, combat stance, weapon handling, additive aim, and transitions share coherent body mechanics.

pieces.name: Light combo
pieces.outcome: Buffered three-hit chain has authored startup, active, recovery, and cancel windows with one-hit-per-target resolution.

pieces.name: Heavy attack
pieces.outcome: Heavy strike communicates commitment, displacement, contact, hitstop, camera impulse, and enemy reaction.

pieces.name: Dodge and evasion
pieces.outcome: Directional dodge, invulnerability window, recovery, and camera continuity are predictable and readable.

pieces.name: Hit reaction and death
pieces.outcome: Zombies react by hit direction and severity, preserve contact, stagger, collapse, and settle without foot sliding or explosive ragdolls.

pieces.name: Zombie navigation
pieces.outcome: One zombie can acquire, approach, flank, telegraph, attack, recover, lose or reacquire, and die without navigation jitter.

pieces.name: Crowd combat director
pieces.outcome: Four-to-six zombies surround without dog-piling; attack tokens, spacing, off-screen pressure, and threat cues create readable crowd combat.

pieces.name: Hero look development
pieces.outcome: The first anime-style fighter reads as a premium authored character at gameplay and finisher distance, with coherent skin, hair, cloth, metal, and weapon materials.

pieces.name: Zombie look development
pieces.outcome: The zombie archetype and variants have layered anatomy, clothing history, damage language, silhouette variation, and material response.

pieces.name: Arena composition
pieces.outcome: A compact arena has foreground framing, combat stage, silhouette depth, traversal logic, landmarks, and no empty test-level read.

pieces.name: Lighting and atmosphere
pieces.outcome: Key, fill, rim, exposure, fog, shadows, grading, and local reactive light keep faces and contact readable while creating depth.

pieces.name: Combat VFX
pieces.outcome: Weapon trails, contact flash, sparks, debris, blood or dust, and lingering particles form a restrained macro, impact, and decay stack anchored to motion.

pieces.name: Combat audio
pieces.outcome: Foley, effort, weapon movement, contact, zombie vocals, ambience, music, ducking, and spatial mix support timing and impact.

pieces.name: HUD and threat language
pieces.outcome: Minimal health, ability, lock-on, and threat information remains legible without weakening the cinematic frame.

pieces.name: Finisher vignette
pieces.outcome: A contextual finisher has reliable setup, three-character blocking when relevant, facial and contact framing, camera choreography, and clean return to play.

pieces.name: Integrated encounter
pieces.outcome: A polished 45–90 second encounter combines the accepted systems into one authored dramatic arc.

pieces.name: Performance and delivery
pieces.outcome: The native macOS target runs reliably, captures deterministically, meets frame budgets, and ships with reproducible build instructions.

pieces.name: Fighter contract
pieces.outcome: Data-driven fighter, weapon, and ability definitions support selection without branching the shared combat core.

pieces.name: Fighter two
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter three
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Fighter four
pieces.outcome: A distinct weapon silhouette, rhythm, traversal or combat ability, animation set, VFX identity, and finisher.

pieces.name: Roster select and persistence
pieces.outcome: Selection, preview, input, save or load, and per-fighter progression work coherently.

pieces.name: Roster encounter balance
pieces.outcome: All fighters can complete the benchmark encounter while remaining mechanically and audiovisually distinct.
